title: Four very different lives, all raised above the worlds.
subtitle: Ismail, Al-Yasa, Yunus and Lut in one line

row.title: preferred
sub: above the people of their time

then: This verse closes a long list of prophets that began with Ibrahim. The Quraysh were pressing the Prophet ﷺ hard in Makkah. Allah names {idea}a whole family of guided people{/idea} who walked the same road before him, and says {reward}each one was preferred above the worlds{/reward}.
now: You scroll past people whose lives look nothing like yours. One stayed in a small town. One ran away and came back. One stood alone against a whole street. {idea}Allah lifted each of them, in a different shape of life.{/idea} Your shape counts too.
old: Only one kind of life is worth honoring, and mine is not it.
new: Allah raised people through very different stories. Mine can be one of them.
try: Read the names in 6:83-86 slowly today. Pick the one whose story you know least and look it up.

title: Guidance ran through fathers, children and brothers.
subtitle: A chosen family line, and a straight path

row.title: Allah chooses
sub: among them, not all of them

then: After naming the prophets, the verse widens to their families. Ibn Kathir notes how Allah placed {reward}prophethood and the Book in the offspring of Nuh and Ibrahim{/reward}. The word is {idea}some of{/idea} them: guidance ran through families, but each person was still chosen.
now: Your grandmother prayed every night. Your cousin memorized Quran. Your brother drifted away. Families carry faith, but {idea}nobody inherits it like a house.{/idea} You can be the link that carries it on, or the one who starts it.
old: My family is religious, so I am covered.
new: A family can carry guidance, but each of us still walks the path ourselves.
try: Ask one older relative how they came to pray. Listen without rushing.

title: Even prophets' deeds would vanish if mixed with shirk.
subtitle: Guidance is Allah's, and shirk cancels everything

row.title: guidance of Allah
sub: He gives it to whom He wills

then: The list of prophets is followed by a startling line. {idea}This is Allah's guidance, His to give.{/idea} And even these chosen men, if they had joined partners with Allah, {trap}all their work would have come to nothing.{/trap} The Quraysh heard it while they worshipped idols beside Allah.
now: You fast, you give, you help at the mosque. Then you catch yourself hoping people notice, or leaning on a charm, a person, a lucky number. {trap}The bricks are only as safe as the ground under them.{/trap} {idea}Keep the ground clean.{/idea}
old: As long as I do a lot of good, the details of who it is for do not matter.
new: Who my deeds are for decides whether they stand at all.
try: Before one good deed today, pause and say quietly: this is for You, Allah.

title: If these people refuse it, others will carry it.
subtitle: The message never depends on one crowd
then: The leaders of Makkah thought that without them the message would die. The verse answers calmly. {reward}Book, wisdom and prophethood{/reward} were given to these prophets. {idea}If these people deny it, Allah has already entrusted it to others{/idea} who will not deny it.
now: You drop the Quran class because work is busy. You tell yourself the group will fall apart. It does not. Someone else steps in. {idea}The work continues with or without you.{/idea} {reward}The honor of carrying it is what you miss.{/reward}
old: If I step back, the good work will collapse.
new: The work will go on. The question is whether I will be part of it.
try: Think of one good thing you quietly stopped doing. Do one small piece of it again this week.

title: Follow their guidance, and ask for nothing in return.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ told to take these men as models
then: After the long list of names, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}these are the ones Allah guided, so follow their guidance.{/idea} Then he is told to say he asks no payment. {reward}It is only a reminder for the worlds.{/reward} Makkah could not accuse him of selling it.
now: You want to grow, so you follow fifty accounts and a dozen gurus. Many of them are selling something. {idea}Here is a short list of people worth copying{/idea}, and the one who brought it asked you for nothing. Start with the ones who did not need your money.
old: I will pick my role models from whoever is loudest right now.
new: The best models are the ones Allah guided, and they asked nothing of me.
try: Pick one prophet from this list. Write down one habit of his you could copy this week.

title: They said Allah never speaks to humans. Then who sent Musa's book?
subtitle: Underestimating Allah, and picking pages from scripture
then: Ibn Abbas and others said this was about the Quraysh, and some said it was about some Jews. They claimed {trap}Allah sends nothing down to any human.{/trap} The reply: then who sent the book Musa brought, {idea}a light and guidance{/idea}, which some had split into pages, showing parts and hiding the rest.
now: You quote the verse that suits you in the argument and skip the one that does not. You screenshot half a hadith for the group chat. {trap}Showing some pages and hiding others{/trap} is easy with a phone. {idea}Take the whole book seriously, including the parts that pinch.{/idea}
old: I can keep the parts of revelation that fit me and quietly skip the rest.
new: Picking pages is a way of not valuing Allah as He deserves.
try: Find one verse you tend to avoid because it asks something of you. Read it with its tafsir today.

title: A blessed Book, and those who believe it guard their prayer.
subtitle: The Quran sent to Makkah and everyone around it
then: Right after the Tawrah, Allah points to {reward}this blessed Book{/reward}, the Quran, sent to warn Makkah, the Mother of Towns, and those around it. Ibn Kathir says that means all people. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and {idea}they keep guarding their prayers.{/idea}
now: You say the Quran matters to you. Then the afternoon meeting runs long and Asr slips by again. {idea}Belief in the next life shows up in a calendar.{/idea} Guarding something means you plan around it, not fit it in.
old: My faith is in my heart, my schedule is a separate thing.
new: Believing in the Hereafter shows in how I protect my prayers.
try: Put the next prayer time in your phone calendar as a meeting you cannot move.

title: Nothing is more unjust than lying in Allah's name.
subtitle: False claims of revelation, and the moment of death
then: Ikrimah and Qatadah said part of this was about Musaylimah, who claimed revelation. Others boasted they could say something like the Quran. The verse calls this {trap}the greatest injustice{/trap}, then shows the moment of death, when the angels tell such people their humiliation comes {trap}for what they said against Allah{/trap} and their arrogance.
now: You hear someone say "Islam says..." about something they just made up. Maybe you have done it, to win an argument or sound sure. {idea}Words about Allah are not small talk.{/idea} It is fine to say "I do not know."
old: Saying what I think religion says is harmless, even if I am not sure.
new: Putting words in Allah's mouth is among the heaviest wrongs there is.
try: Next time you are unsure what Islam says on something, say I do not know, and look it up later.

title: You come back alone, the way you first came.
subtitle: Everything given is left behind on that Day
then: On the Day of Return it will be said: {idea}you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith where the son of Adam says "my money, my money," yet {reward}he only keeps what he ate, wore, or gave in charity.{/reward} The idols they relied on are nowhere.
now: Moving house, you see how much stuff you own. Boxes of it. Now picture leaving with nothing in your hands. {idea}No phone, no contacts, no one to vouch for you.{/idea} {reward}What you gave away is the only thing already packed.{/reward}
old: What I build up and who I know will carry me.
new: I arrive alone, and only what I sent ahead is waiting.
try: Give away one thing today you were keeping just to keep it.

title: He splits the seed and brings life out of dead things.
subtitle: Recognizing Allah in a sprouting grain
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah makes {idea}the lifeless seed and fruit stone split and sprout{/idea}, giving many kinds of plants. He brings life from what is dead and the dead from the living. {idea}That is Allah{/idea}, so how could the people of Makkah be turned away to worshipping others?
now: A chickpea left in a damp jar on the windowsill. Three days later, a tiny white root. You have seen it a hundred times and never stopped. {idea}Something dry and dead pushed out a living thing.{/idea} That is a signature.
old: Seeds sprouting is just science, nothing to think about.
new: Every sprout is Allah bringing life out of something dead, right in front of me.
try: Soak a few seeds or lentils in water tonight. Watch them over the next days and say SubhanAllah when they open.

title: He breaks the dawn and gives the night for rest.
subtitle: Day, night, sun and moon on exact measure

row.title: rest
sub: a gift built into the day

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is the Creator of light and darkness. {reward}He splits the darkness with dawn{/reward} and makes the night still so creatures can rest. The sun and moon run fixed courses that set seasons and the length of days. {idea}This is the measuring of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.{/idea}
now: It is 1 a.m. and you are still scrolling, telling yourself you will sleep soon. {reward}The night was made for rest, on purpose.{/reward} {trap}You keep fighting a gift.{/trap} Sunrise tomorrow will come on time, whether you are ready or not.
old: Night is just extra time I can use however I want.
new: Night is a gift of rest, measured out by the One who knows what I need.
try: Tonight put your phone in another room thirty minutes before you sleep.

title: Stars were placed to guide you through the dark.
subtitle: Signs laid out in detail for people who know
then: The Arabs crossed deserts and seas by night, steering by the stars. Allah says {idea}He placed them so you could find your way in the dark.{/idea} Ibn Kathir quotes some of the early scholars: stars are for {reward}beauty, guarding the sky, and direction{/reward}, and anyone who claims more has made a mistake.
now: Your phone shows your horoscope next to the weather. Half joking, you read it. {idea}The stars were made to guide your feet, not to run your future.{/idea} The same sky that guided caravans is still pointing to the One who set it there.
old: The stars might say something about my luck.
new: The stars are signs that guide, pointing me back to Allah who placed them.
try: Step outside tonight, find one star, and thank Allah for one way He guided you this year.

title: One soul for all of us, then a stay and a storage.
subtitle: One origin, and the places we pass through
then: Ibn Kathir says the single soul is Adam. The scholars explained the two words in different ways: {idea}a place of stay in the womb and a place of storage in the father's loins{/idea}, or this life and the grave after it. Either way, {idea}every person has stations they pass through.{/idea}
now: The cleaner at your office, the stranger on the bus, the cousin you avoid at weddings. {idea}Same first father.{/idea} And each of you is only passing through this station. The grave is the next stop for all of you.
old: People who are not like me are a different kind of human.
new: We all come from one soul and pass through the same stations.
try: Greet someone today you normally walk past without a word.

title: Look at the fruit as it forms and as it ripens.
subtitle: Rain, grain, dates, grapes, olives, pomegranates
then: Ibn Kathir notes dates and grapes were the most precious fruits to the people of the Hijaz. Allah describes them hanging low, easy to pick, with olives and pomegranates whose leaves look alike but whose fruit differs. Then a direct command: {idea}look at the fruit when it forms and when it ripens.{/idea} {reward}In this are signs for people who believe.{/reward}
now: You grab a pomegranate at the supermarket without looking. Same water, same soil, yet each fruit has its own color and taste. {idea}The verse literally tells you to look.{/idea} Slow down at the fruit stand once.
old: Fruit is just food. There is nothing to see in it.
new: Every fruit is a sign, if I actually stop and look at it.
try: Before you eat a piece of fruit today, look at it for ten seconds and think about where it came from.

title: They made partners of the jinn He created.
subtitle: Inventing sons and daughters for Allah without knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the idol worshippers {trap}obeyed the jinn who told them to worship idols{/trap}, so in effect they worshipped the jinn. They also invented children for Allah, like the pagan claim that angels were His daughters. The answer is short: {idea}He created them.{/idea} How can a creation share the Creator's place?
now: You would never call anything a god. But there is a voice you obey even when you know it is wrong. A craving, an influencer, the fear of what people say. {trap}Obeying it is a kind of worship.{/trap} {idea}It too is just something Allah created.{/idea}
old: Shirk is about statues, nothing to do with me.
new: Whatever I obey against Allah is taking a place only the Creator deserves.
try: Notice one voice today that pulls you against what you know is right. Name it, and say: Allah created you.
